# Agent-readiness rubric

Fourteen evidence-based maturity ratings describe repository capabilities.
Levels identify realistic next transitions; confidence remains separate.
A documented command is not proof of its successful execution. Missing or
truncated evidence is unknown, not level zero. The progressive-disclosure
mapping applies the shared progression to the existing disclosure principle.

## context-discovery

- Level 0 — Implicit: Project rules live only in people's heads, chat history, or scattered PR comments. No file an agent would read on its own states them.
- Level 1 — Discoverable: A root-level file (README, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or equivalent) exists and states the basics, but may be incomplete or drift out of date.
- Level 2 — Usable: The entry-point file accurately covers build, test, and key conventions; an agent can act on it directly without trial and error.
- Level 3 — Integrated: Discovery is scoped — nested/linked instructions for subprojects, links to architecture and domain docs — so an agent loads only what its current task needs.
- Level 4 — Adaptive: Gaps found during real work (an agent hits an undocumented constraint) feed back into updating the entry-point docs, closing the loop.

## progressive-disclosure

- Level 0 — Implicit: Guidance is monolithic or requires loading unrelated detail before work can begin.
- Level 1 — Discoverable: Entry points distinguish summary guidance from supporting detail.
- Level 2 — Usable: Linked guidance lets an agent load the relevant detail for common tasks.
- Level 3 — Integrated: Layered guidance follows workflow and subsystem boundaries and stays current with changes.
- Level 4 — Adaptive: Evidence of missing context or excessive context feeds back into better layering and routing.

# Catalog agent guide
Read README.md for setup, docs/architecture.md for module boundaries and docs/domain.md for domain terms before changing catalog behavior. Use pnpm for packages. Changes need a small plan, focused tests and review before merge. Ask the maintainer before API changes, data deletion or publishing. Document lessons in docs/lessons.md. No autonomous deployment.

name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm test

# Catalog library
A TypeScript library that stores product inventory in memory. Node 22 and pnpm 11.24.0. Setup: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Verification: pnpm test. No services, network access or secrets required. Agent entry point: AGENTS.md. Architecture: docs/architecture.md. Domain glossary: docs/domain.md. No recorded verification results are available.

# Architecture
The public createCatalog factory in src/catalog.ts owns the in-memory product map. add validates the product identifier and stock count before storage. The catalog has no I/O boundary, database or deployment component. src/catalog.test.ts describes invalid input and duplicate behavior.

# Domain glossary
A Product is a catalog entry with a unique nonempty SKU string and a nonnegative integer stock count. SKU means stock keeping unit; it is case-sensitive and is not a display label. A Catalog owns products keyed by SKU. Adding an existing SKU is an error, never an update. Stock is the count of individual available units, not currency or a reservation. Negative and fractional stock are invalid. src/catalog.ts add enforces these invariants and src/catalog.test.ts encodes the duplicate, negative and fractional cases. There is no persistence, order or reservation model.

# Lessons
No completed task outcomes have been recorded. This file is the designated place for durable lessons; there is no automated feedback or curation process.

data.summary: Documentation supports discoverable context, linked architecture and domain guidance, documented setup and verification, and explicit oversight expectations. CI configuration and recorded test assertions establish intent and scoped test-body evidence, not observed reliability. Lessons storage exists without completed outcomes.
